To color table rows in LaTeX you normally use `\rowcolor` from the `xcolor` (or `colortbl`) package.

### 1. Basic setup

```latex
\usepackage[table]{xcolor} % put this in the preamble
```

### 2. Color a single row

```latex
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
\hline
\rowcolor{gray!20}
Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\ \hline
A & B & C \\ \hline
D & E & F \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
```

- `gray!20` means 20% gray (lighter).
- You can use predefined colors (`red`, `blue`, `green`, etc.) or define your own:
  ```latex
  \definecolor{lightblue}{RGB}{220,230,255}
  ```

### 3. Color alternating rows

```latex
\rowcolors{2}{gray!15}{white} % from row 2, alternate gray/white
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
\hline
Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\ \hline
A & B & C \\
D & E & F \\
G & H & I \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\rowcolors{2}{}{} % reset if needed
```

### 4. Color starting from a specific column

You can start the color from a certain column using an optional argument:

```latex
\rowcolor{yellow!30}[1] % color from column 1 onward (default)
\rowcolor{yellow!30}[2] % color from column 2 onward
```

Example:

```latex
\begin{tabular}{l l l}
\rowcolor{yellow!30}[2]
A & B & C \\
D & E & F \\
\end{tabular}
```
